title: User B reuses user A's 6,000-token prefix at 0.1×, until a timestamp on top breaks every hit
subtitle: Example: a made-up app scores videos against each user's goal, with the real rules of Anthropic's prompt caching.

steps.label:
fixed rules, 6,000 tokens ▸ marker
then goal + videos, 900 tokens

outcome.title: Every call pays the 1.25× write, and nothing is read
lines: Put changing values last. In the example day of 10,000 calls, that is about $225 against about $18 cached.

captions.title: Put the fixed text first and mark its end
captions.text: Tools, then the 6,000-token system prompt with a `cache_control` marker at its end. The user's goal and videos, 900 tokens, go last with no marker. `ephemeral` means 5 minutes, `"ttl": "1h"` one hour.

captions.title: User A misses, so the provider stores the prefix
captions.text: Nothing is cached yet, so the provider processes all 6,900 tokens and keeps its work over the 6,000-token prefix. The usage says write 6,000, read 0, input 900. Storing costs 1.25× the input price.

captions.title: User B hits and pays a tenth for the prefix
captions.text: Within 5 minutes, user B's request starts with the same 6,000 tokens. The provider reads them at 0.1× the input price on most models and replies sooner. Every hit restarts the 5-minute clock.

captions.title: Log three counts to prove it works
captions.text: The usage splits input into read 6,000, write 0 and input 900. The read share is 6,000 / 6,900 ≈ 87%. It cannot reach 100% while an uncached tail exists, so 87% is healthy.

captions.title: A timestamp at the top breaks every hit
captions.text: The match must be exact from the first token. "Now 14:02" (made up) on top makes every prefix new, so every call pays the 1.25× write and nothing is read. Tools in a different order on each call break it the same way.
